Title: Diagnosis Details: The test that failed is `testUnion()` in `DOMModelTest`, checking the XPath expression `/vendor[1]/contact[4] | /vendor[1]/contact[1]` should yield the value "John". The core issue, described in the bug report, is that the union operation does not sort the nodes in document order after merging node sets. The specification for the XPath `string()` function requires that when converting node-sets to strings, the string-value of the first node in document order should be returned. The example XML `
avaluebvalue
` and XPath `string(/MAIN/B | /MAIN/A)` should return "avalue" because `` appears before `` in the document. The actual value returned was "bvalue", indicating the document order was not respected. The union operation is likely implemented in the class `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.TreeCompiler` which constructs a `CoreOperationUnion` object for the union of expressions. However, the underlying faulty behavior seems localized to the DOM model's handling of unioned node sets. Attempts to fetch the method `union` on `DOMModel` failed but hints from the current report and the failed test indicate the union implementation merges node sets but neglects to sort the combined nodes according to their document order. Recent bug reports mention issues with node-set comparisons but do not directly mention union sorting. In conclusion, after unioning two node sets, the nodes are not sorted to ensure the first node in document order is at the front. This leads to an incorrect node order and therefore incorrect string conversions or retrievals when using unioned node-sets. The fix should involve ensuring the union operation returns a node iterator containing nodes sorted according to document order. Next, I will verify if the `CoreOperationUnion` or related node iterator returned by the union operation does any sorting post union.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
